33667-two-prisoners.creator: Thomas Nelson Page
33667-two-prisoners.description: A book by Thomas Nelson Page. ature, who said she had once been "a wash lady," but who had long given up a profession which required such constant use of water, and who now, so far as could be seen, used no liquid in any way except whiskey or beer.

72402-the-klygha.title: The Klygha
72402-the-klygha.creator: Unknown
72402-the-klygha.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The Terran bends in a strange way, to rest himself on a place shaped for that. So does the Klygha, but _he_ looks and bends differently when he sees his reflection within his travelling-shell. The Terran is bigger and thicker, and his skin is tighter.

arxiv-2110-09153.title: Probabilistic Inference in Planning for Partially Observable Long Horizon Problems
arxiv-2110-09153.creator: Alphonsus Adu-Bredu Nikhil Devraj Pin-Han Lin Zhen Zeng Odest Chadwicke Jenkins
arxiv-2110-09153.description: Abstract For autonomous service robots to successfully perform long horizon tasks in the real world, they must act intelligently in partially observable environments. Most Task and Motion Planning approaches assume full observability of their state space, making them ineffective in stochastic and partially observable domains that reflect the uncertainties in the real world.

arxiv-2202-04945.title: Computability of finite simplicial complexes
arxiv-2202-04945.creator: Djamel Eddine Amir, Mathieu Hoyrup
arxiv-2202-04945.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Djamel Eddine Amir, Mathieu Hoyrup. The topological properties of a set have a strong impact on its computability properties. A striking illustration of this idea is given by spheres and closed manifolds: if a set X X is homeomorphic to a sphere or a closed manifold, then any algorithm that semicomputes X X in some sense can be converted into an algorithm that fully computes X X .

arxiv-2206-02266.title: Information Threshold, Bayesian Inference and Decision-Making
arxiv-2206-02266.creator: Dr. Jacques Balayla MD, MPH
arxiv-2206-02266.description: Abstract We define the information threshold as the point of maximum curvature in the prior vs. posterior Bayesian curve, both of which are described as a function of the true positive and negative rates of the classification system in question.

arxiv-2304-14411.title: Classifier for centrality determination with Zero Degree Calorimeter at the Cooling-Storage-Ring External-target Experiment
arxiv-2304-14411.creator: Biao Zhang, Li-Ke Liu, Hua Pei, Shusu Shi, Nu Xu, Yaping Wang
arxiv-2304-14411.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Biao Zhang, Li-Ke Liu, Hua Pei, Shusu Shi, Nu Xu, Yaping Wang. The Zero Degree Calorimeter (ZDC) plays a crucial role in determining centrality at the Cooling-Storage-Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) in the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL). A Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) multi-classification algorithm is employed to classify the centrality of the collision events based on the raw features from ZDC such as the number of fired channels and deposited energy.

arxiv-2409-07505.title: A Survey of Anomaly Detection in In-Vehicle Networks
arxiv-2409-07505.creator: Övgü Özdemir, M. Tuğberk İşyapar, Pınar Karagöz, Klaus Werner Schmidt, Demet Demir, N. Alpay Karagöz
arxiv-2409-07505.description: Abstract Modern vehicles are equipped with Electronic Control Units (ECU) that are used for controlling important vehicle functions including safety-critical operations. ECUs exchange information via in-vehicle communication buses, of which the Controller Area Network (CAN bus) is by far the most widespread representative.

arxiv-2510-08756.title: Constraining the Cosmological Evolution of Post-Newtonian Parameters with Gravitational Wave Signals from Compact Binary Inspirals
arxiv-2510-08756.creator: Oliver Pitt, Timothy Clifton
arxiv-2510-08756.description: Abstract Gravitational waves from compact binary inspirals offer a new opportunity to constrain the cosmological time dependence of gravitational coupling parameters, due to the high precision of the observations themselves as well as the significant cosmological redshifts at which such systems exist.

gao-gaoreports-b-308968.title: B-308968, No-Cost Contracts for Event Planning Services, November 27, 2007
gao-gaoreports-b-308968.creator: U.S. Government Accountability Office
gao-gaoreports-b-308968.description: B-308968, No-Cost Contracts for Event Planning Services, November 27, 2007 (2007).

pmc-10543222.title: Luminescence of carbon quantum dots and their application in biochemistry
pmc-10543222.creator: Haili Bao, Yihao Liu, He Li, Wenxin Qi, Keyan Sun
pmc-10543222.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Similar to fullerenes, carbon nanotubes and graphene, carbon dots (CDs) are causing a lot of research work in their own right. CDs are a type of surface-passivated quantum dot that contain carbon atoms. Their distinctive characteristics, such as luminescent emission that varies with size and wavelength, resistance to photobleaching, easy biological binding, lack of toxicity, and economical production without the need for intricate synthetic processes, have led to a noteworthy surge in attention within the research community.

pmc-10598231.title: Performance of baseline FDG-PET/CT radiomics for prediction of bone marrow minimal residual disease status in the LyMa-101 trial
pmc-10598231.creator: Caroline Bodet-Milin, Cyrille Morvant, Thomas Carlier, Gauthier Frecon, Olivier Tournilhac, Violaine Safar, Françoise Kraeber-Bodere, Steven Le Gouill, Elizabeth Macintyre, Clément Bailly
pmc-10598231.description: The prognostic value of 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) at baseline or the predictive value of minimal residual disease (MRD) detection appear as potential tools to improve mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) patients’ management. The LyMa-101, a phase 2 trial of the LYSA group (ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT02896582) reported induction therapy with obinutuzumab, a CD20 monoclonal antibody.

pmc-10700409.title: A multitask deep learning radiomics model for predicting the macrotrabecular-massive subtype and prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma after hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy
pmc-10700409.creator: Xuelei He, Kai Li, Ran Wei, Mengxuan Zuo, Wang Yao, Zechen Zheng, Xiaowei He, Yan Fu, Chengzhi Li, Chao An, Wendao Liu
pmc-10700409.description: BackgroundThe macrotrabecular-massive (MTM) is a special subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which has commonly a dismal prognosis. This study aimed to develop a multitask deep learning radiomics (MDLR) model for predicting MTM and HCC patients’ prognosis after hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC).

pmc-11377688.title: Evaluation of atmospheric-plasma-source absorption mode Fourier transform Orbitrap mass spectrometry for chlorinated paraffin mixtures
pmc-11377688.creator: Claudia Masucci, Konstantin O. Nagornov, Anton N. Kozhinov, Kevin Kraft, Yury O. Tsybin, Davide Bleiner
pmc-11377688.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chlorinated paraffins (CP) are complex molecular mixtures occurring in a wide range of isomers and homologs of environmental hazards, whose analytical complexity demand advanced mass spectrometry (MS) methods for their characterization. The reported formation of chlorinated olefins (COs) and other transformation products during CP biotransformation and degradation can alter the MS analysis, increasing the high resolution required to distinguish CPs from their degradation products.

pmc-11713332.title: Study partner‐reported decline as a predictor of diagnostic progression in underrepresented populations in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohort
pmc-11713332.creator: Amanda T Calcetas, Alyssa Arentoft, Hyunjung Lee, Heining Cham, Miriam T Ashford, Adam Diaz, Adeyinka Ajayi, Omobolanle Ayo, Alicia M Camuy, Julia E Culhane, Kaori Kubo Germano, Vanessa A Guzman, Shaniya Parkins, Sandra Talavera, Monica Rivera Mindt
pmc-11713332.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIt is imperative to identify underrepresented populations (URPs) at risk for progression to Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet substantial heterogeneity exists in the presentation and risk of AD among URPs. Previous research with predominantly non‐Latinx White participants indicates early functional decline is associated with increased risk and can be effectively evaluated by participants and study partners (SPs). This study aims to understand the association between subjective functional/cognitive decline and objectively‐measured cognitive decline in URPs.

pmc-12387745.title: Resting-State Electroencephalogram (EEG) as a Biomarker of Learning Disabilities in Children—A Systematic Review
pmc-12387745.creator: James Chmiel, Jarosław Nadobnik, Szymon Smerdel, Mirela Niedzielska, Syoichi Tashiro
pmc-12387745.description: Introduction: Learning disabilities (LD) compromise academic achievement in approximately 5–10% of school-aged children, yet the neurophysiological signatures that could facilitate earlier detection or stratification remain poorly defined. Resting-state electroencephalography (rs-EEG) offers millisecond resolution and is cost-effective, but its findings have never been synthesized systematically across pediatric LD cohorts.

pmc-12574240.title: A study protocol on assessing the acceptance and effectiveness of a digital adherence technology for TB preventive treatment in Bangladesh
pmc-12574240.creator: Pushpita Samina, Md Rifat Haidar, Tasmia Ibrahim, Tanjina Rahman, Mohammad Shahnewaz Sarker, Syada Samsia Noor, Shahriar Ahmed, Mohammad Khaja Mafij Uddin, Senjuti Kabir, Sayera Banu
pmc-12574240.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAdherence to tuberculosis(TB) preventive treatment (TPT) remains a significant challenge in high-TB burden countries like Bangladesh, where approximately 44 million people are infected with latent tuberculosis.Methods/DesignThis study protocol describes a mixed-methods observational study to evaluate “iDOTS,” a locally developed digital adherence technology adapted from 99DOTS, for monitoring and improving TPT adherence among adult household contacts of bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB patients.

pmc-12584900.title: Current diagnostic approach to fungal infection in the critically ill patient
pmc-12584900.creator: Alfredo Maldonado-Barrueco, Inmaculada Quiles-Melero, Julio García-Rodríguez
pmc-12584900.description: Invasive fungal infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, with an increasing global incidence and species diversity, especially after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. Diagnosis relies on a combination of classical methods (microscopy, culture) and non-classical tools including biomarkers (1,3-β-D-glucan, galactomannan, mannan) and molecular assays.

pmc-13088331.title: Ethnic Bridging of Sepiapterin in Chinese and Korean Populations Based on Predictions From Genetic Polymorphism of Breast Cancer Resistance Protein
pmc-13088331.creator: Lan Gao, Neil Smith, Ronald Kong
pmc-13088331.description: Ethnic differences are crucial when considering the efficacy, safety, and dose of pharmaceuticals across diverse populations. The International Council for Harmonization of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) guideline E5 addresses the acceptability of extrapolating foreign clinical data taking ethnic factors into consideration.

pmc-13115749.title: Antifungal Activity and Biochemical Mechanisms of Artemisinin Against the Phytopathogen Sclerotinia sclerotiorum
pmc-13115749.creator: Yuxin Zhao, Xin Li, Hai-Ning Lyu, Jingjing Liao, Jiale Xing, Xin Zhao, Qian Zhang, Huanling Yang, Shuyu Li, Junzhe Zhang, Qiaoli Shi, Chengchao Xu, Xin Chai
pmc-13115749.description: Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (Lib.) de Bary is a globally distributed necrotrophic fungal pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of crops. While conventional chemical fungicides offer effective control, their long-term use leads to increased fungicide resistance and poses risks to the environment and human health due to pesticide residues, underscoring the urgent need to develop novel fungicides.

pmc-13208683.title: Subclinical Inflammation in Ischemic Heart Disease and Its Role in the Transition to Heart Failure
pmc-13208683.creator: Costin Petru Groza, Ovidiu Oita, Radu Sebastian Gavril, Oana Irina Gavril, Tatiana Dramba, Ionica Grigore, Cristina Strobescu-Ciobanu, Roxana Nemtanu, Irina Mihaela Esanu
pmc-13208683.description: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) remains the leading cause of chronic heart failure (HF) worldwide, yet the biological processes underlying this transition are not fully elucidated. Growing evidence indicates that chronic, low-grade inflammation acts as a pivotal link between ischemic injury and progressive myocardial dysfunction.

pmc-13382530.title: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type 2 Vpx-mediated Degradation of TASOR Activates Innate Immune Sensing of Nucleic Acids in Infected Cells
pmc-13382530.creator: Heather M Hanson, Madeline R Damkot, Louis M Mansky
pmc-13382530.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The HIV-2/SIVsm lineage of lentiviruses encodes for Vpx, which is a virus-associated protein that is absent from HIV-1. Vpx enhances HIV-2 replication by degrading host proteins that possess antiviral activity. For example, Vpx is known to degrade the host dNTPase SAMHD1 (which reduces dNTP levels to inhibit viral DNA synthesis in macrophages) and components of the epigenetic regulator complex HUSH (where degradation enhances proviral gene expression and viral replication).

pmc-13435436.title: Thyroid nodule and autoimmune thyroid disease frequency in adults with inborn errors of immunity: a case-control study
pmc-13435436.creator: Zeliha Yarar, Mehmet Emin Gerek, Fatih Çölkesen, Şevket Arslan, Feridun Karakurt
pmc-13435436.description: BackgroundInborn errors of immunity (IEIs) are defined by impaired immune function and abnormal immune system development. The recognition of significant interactions between the immune and endocrine systems has emerged as an area of growing clinical interest. The study aimed to evaluate the frequency of thyroid nodules and autoimmune thyroid diseases in patients with IEIs.

pmc-13658628.title: Common Data Elements for Preclinical High-Frequency Oscillations in Epilepsy
pmc-13658628.creator: Ziyi Wang, JiaoJiao Guo, Christos Panagiotis Lisgaras
pmc-13658628.description: Normal brain function relies on coordinated oscillations within and across neural circuits. In epilepsy, disruption of these oscillations may reflect pathological excitability associated with seizure generation and/or the emergence of comorbidities. Among these oscillatory activities, high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, typically within 80-500 Hz) are increasingly considered promising electrophysiological biomarkers of epileptogenicity.
